# 12. Cross-method TF consistency

This section integrates **every TF result generated above** for the LNCaP
LOY-vs-sgCTRL contrast — seven methods × one contrast — and asks:
**which TFs are flagged consistently across methods, and which are
single-method outliers?**

The seven methods span three regulon resources and three inference engines:

| # | Method                | Regulon source                  | Inference   |
|---|-----------------------|----------------------------------|-------------|
| 1 | DoRothEA              | DoRothEA pancancer A/B/C        | fgsea       |
| 2 | decoupleR_CollecTRI   | CollecTRI                       | ULM         |
| 3 | decoupleR_TRRUST      | TRRUST v2 (literature, curated) | ULM         |
| 4 | msVIPER_CollecTRI     | CollecTRI                       | msVIPER     |
| 5 | msVIPER_ARACNe        | TCGA-PRAD ARACNe (tissue-matched)| msVIPER    |
| 6 | msVIPER_TRRUST        | TRRUST v2                       | msVIPER     |
| 7 | msVIPER_TFT           | MSigDB C3:TFT:GTRD (ChIP)       | msVIPER     |

LNCaP has no PARENTAL arm and no pooled-baseline contrast, so the cross-method
agreement on the single LOY-vs-sgCTRL contrast is the only consistency axis
available here. Cross-cell-line agreement against the A549 and HT1080 robust
hits is deferred to the combined analysis (`2.4_rnaseq_combined.Rmd`).

## 12.1 Aggregate all TF NES results

```{r tf-consistency-collect}
# Normalize each source to a common 4-column long format:
#   TF, NES, sig, source
to_long <- function(df, tf_col, val_col, sig_expr, source_lab) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      TF     = .data[[tf_col]],
      NES    = .data[[val_col]],
      sig    = !!sig_expr,
      source = source_lab
    )
}

tf_long <- bind_rows(
  to_long(tf_gsea_lc,              "pathway", "NES",   rlang::expr(padj < 0.05),
          "DoRothEA"),
  to_long(contrast_acts_lc,        "source",  "score", rlang::expr(p_value < 0.05),
          "decoupleR_CollecTRI"),
  to_long(contrast_acts_trrust_lc, "source",  "score", rlang::expr(p_value < 0.05),
          "decoupleR_TRRUST"),
  to_long(msv_lc_col,              "TF",      "NES",   rlang::expr(FDR < 0.05),
          "msVIPER_CollecTRI"),
  to_long(msv_lc_arc,              "TF",      "NES",   rlang::expr(FDR < 0.05),
          "msVIPER_ARACNe"),
  to_long(msv_lc_trrust,           "TF",      "NES",   rlang::expr(FDR < 0.05),
          "msVIPER_TRRUST"),
  to_long(msv_lc_tft,              "TF",      "NES",   rlang::expr(FDR < 0.05),
          "msVIPER_TFT")
)

fwrite(tf_long, file.path(TF_DIR, "lncap_tf_consistency_long.csv"))

tf_long %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarize(tested = n(),
            sig    = sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "TF result counts by source (LOY vs sgCTRL)")
```

## 12.2 Consistency heatmap (top robust TFs)

Score each TF by how many of the **seven methods** flag it as significant
(max = 7). Heatmap the NES of the top scorers across all seven method columns.

```{r tf-consistency-heatmap, fig.height=12, fig.width=9}
tf_score <- tf_long %>%
  group_by(TF) %>%
  summarize(
    sig_count          = sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE),
    abs_NES_mean       = mean(abs(NES), na.rm = TRUE),
    NES_direction_mean = mean(NES, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(sig_count), desc(abs_NES_mean))

# Pick TFs hit by >=4 of 7 methods, clamp to 40 for plot readability
top_tfs_consistent <- tf_score %>%
  dplyr::filter(sig_count >= 4) %>%
  slice_head(n = 40) %>%
  pull(TF)

cat(sprintf("TFs significant in >=4 of 7 methods: %d (showing top %d)\n",
            sum(tf_score$sig_count >= 4), length(top_tfs_consistent)))

if (length(top_tfs_consistent) > 0) {
  hm_cells <- expand.grid(
    TF     = top_tfs_consistent,
    source = c("DoRothEA",
               "decoupleR_CollecTRI", "decoupleR_TRRUST",
               "msVIPER_CollecTRI",   "msVIPER_ARACNe",
               "msVIPER_TRRUST",      "msVIPER_TFT"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  hm_full <- hm_cells %>%
    left_join(tf_long %>% dplyr::select(TF, source, NES, sig),
              by = c("TF", "source")) %>%
    mutate(
      TF         = factor(TF, levels = rev(top_tfs_consistent)),
      source     = factor(source, levels = unique(hm_cells$source)),
      sig_marker = ifelse(isTRUE(sig) | (!is.na(sig) & sig), "*", "")
    )

  p_consist_hm <- ggplot(hm_full, aes(x = source, y = TF, fill = NES)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sig_marker), color = "black",
              size = 3.5, vjust = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#0072B2", mid = "grey92", high = "#D55E00",
                         midpoint = 0, na.value = "grey80",
                         name = "NES / score") +
    labs(title = sprintf("TF cross-method consistency (top %d robust TFs)",
                         length(top_tfs_consistent)),
         subtitle = "LOY vs sgCTRL; * = significant in that method.",
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 8),
      panel.grid  = element_blank(),
      plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  print(p_consist_hm)
  save_fig(p_consist_hm, "tf_consistency_heatmap",
           width = 7, height = 10)
} else {
  cat("No TF reached significance in >=2 methods.\n")
}
```

## 12.3 Robust hits — TFs flagged by multiple methods

Robust hits: TFs significant in at least **five of the seven methods**. The
direction (NES sign) is also reported so up- and down-regulated TFs can be
read separately.

```{r tf-robust-hits}
sig_methods <- function(tf) {
  tf_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(TF == tf, sig) %>%
    dplyr::pull(source) %>% unique()
}

robust_tbl <- tf_score %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    sig_sources = paste(sig_methods(TF), collapse = ", "),
    n_methods   = length(sig_methods(TF))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_methods >= 5) %>%
  arrange(desc(sig_count), desc(abs_NES_mean))

cat(sprintf("Robust LNCaP LOY TFs (significant in >=5 of 7 methods): %d\n",
            nrow(robust_tbl)))

fwrite(robust_tbl, file.path(TF_DIR, "lncap_tf_robust_hits.csv"))

if (nrow(robust_tbl) > 0) {
  robust_tbl %>%
    dplyr::select(TF, sig_count, NES_direction_mean, sig_sources) %>%
    head(30) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 2,
                 caption = "Top 30 robust LNCaP LOY TFs (>=5 of 7 methods agree)")
} else {
  cat("No TF met the strict robust-hit criteria.\n")
}
```

***

# 13. Label-permutation null

How much of what we see in §4–§12 is real biology vs. method-level noise? This
section shuffles the **treatment labels** (LOY ↔ sgCTRL) across samples
*N* times, re-runs the canonical pipeline on each shuffle (unpaired limma–voom
DE → Hallmark fgsea → decoupleR ULM TF activity on CollecTRI), and asks:
**how often does a random labeling produce as many DEGs / enriched pathways /
significant TFs as the real assignment?**

The DE design here is **unpaired** for both the observed reference value and
the null — many shuffles place both LOY samples in the same passage and would
otherwise yield rank-deficient paired designs. An unpaired null is the fair
head-to-head and is generally more permissive (more variance to explain), so
finding the real result extreme against it is conservative.

## 13.1 Setup

```{r perm-setup}
N_PERM <- 100
PERM_SEED <- 42
set.seed(PERM_SEED)

# Original treatment vector (full DGEList, before any contrast subset)
real_treatment <- as.character(dge$samples$treatment)
real_passage   <- as.character(dge$samples$passage)

# Each permutation reassigns the existing per-class sample counts across
# the same samples (so n_LOY, n_CTRL stay fixed; only WHICH samples carry
# each label changes).
perm_seeds <- seq_len(N_PERM)
cat(sprintf("N permutations: %d   |   class sizes preserved: %s\n",
            N_PERM, paste(names(table(real_treatment)),
                          table(real_treatment), sep = "=",
                          collapse = ", ")))
```

## 13.2 Helpers

```{r perm-helpers}
# Run one permutation: returns N_DEG, N_GSEA, N_TF for shuffled labels.
# `dge_full` is the full DGEList (pre-filtered, Y-removed, TMM-normalized).
run_one_perm <- function(shuf_trt, dge_full, net_obj, hallmark_sets) {
  keep <- shuf_trt %in% c("CTRL", "LOY")
  s_dge <- dge_full[, keep, keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
  s_trt <- factor(shuf_trt[keep], levels = c("CTRL", "LOY"))

  # Unpaired DE
  s_dge <- calcNormFactors(s_dge, method = "TMM")
  des <- model.matrix(~ 0 + s_trt)
  colnames(des) <- gsub("^s_trt", "", colnames(des))
  cm  <- makeContrasts(contrasts = "LOY - CTRL", levels = colnames(des))
  v   <- voom(s_dge, des, plot = FALSE)
  fit <- lmFit(v, des) %>% contrasts.fit(cm) %>% eBayes()
  tt  <- topTable(fit, coef = 1, n = Inf, sort.by = "P")
  tt$gene_name <- s_dge$genes[rownames(tt), "gene_name"]

  n_deg <- sum(tt$adj.P.Val < ALPHA & abs(tt$logFC) > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Hallmark fgsea — same rank construction as §5 (symbol-keyed t-stat,
  # collapse duplicates by |max|, RPS/RPL excluded)
  rdf <- tt %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(gene_name), nzchar(gene_name), !is.na(t)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gene_name) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(stat = t[which.max(abs(t))], .groups = "drop")
  rdf <- rdf[!grepl("^RPS\\d|^RPL\\d", rdf$gene_name), ]
  rdf <- rdf[!rdf$gene_name %in% par_gene_names, ]  # drop PAR for pathway/TF
  r <- setNames(rdf$stat, rdf$gene_name)
  r <- sort(r, decreasing = TRUE)

  set.seed(42)  # fgsea internal sampling seeded for reproducibility
  fres <- suppressWarnings(fgsea(pathways = hallmark_sets, stats = r,
                                  minSize = 15, maxSize = 500))
  n_gsea <- sum(fres$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

  # decoupleR ULM on CollecTRI with the same t-stat vector
  deg_mat <- matrix(rdf$stat, ncol = 1,
                    dimnames = list(rdf$gene_name, "stat"))
  acts <- suppressMessages(run_ulm(
    mat = deg_mat, net = net_obj,
    .source = "source", .target = "target", .mor = "mor", minsize = 5))
  n_tf <- sum(acts$p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

  list(n_deg = n_deg, n_gsea = n_gsea, n_tf = n_tf)
}

# Wrapper: returns observed metrics using the real label vector for a fair
# head-to-head against the null (unpaired DE; same rank/fgsea/ULM settings).
real_perm <- run_one_perm(real_treatment, dge,
                          net, pathways$hallmark)
cat(sprintf("Observed (unpaired, real labels):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  N_DEG (FDR<%g, |lfc|>%g): %d\n",
            ALPHA, LFC_THR, real_perm$n_deg))
cat(sprintf("  N_Hallmark (padj<0.05):   %d\n", real_perm$n_gsea))
cat(sprintf("  N_TF (CollecTRI ULM p<0.05): %d\n", real_perm$n_tf))
```

## 13.3 Run permutations

```{r perm-run, cache=TRUE}
perm_out <- lapply(perm_seeds, function(s) {
  set.seed(PERM_SEED + s)
  shuf <- sample(real_treatment)
  run_one_perm(shuf, dge, net, pathways$hallmark)
})

null_df <- tibble::tibble(
  perm  = seq_len(N_PERM),
  n_deg  = vapply(perm_out, `[[`, integer(1), "n_deg"),
  n_gsea = vapply(perm_out, `[[`, integer(1), "n_gsea"),
  n_tf   = vapply(perm_out, `[[`, integer(1), "n_tf"))

fwrite(null_df, file.path(TF_DIR, "lncap_permutation_null.csv"))

cat("Permutation summary (median [10th–90th percentile]):\n")
for (m in c("n_deg", "n_gsea", "n_tf")) {
  q <- quantile(null_df[[m]], c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("  %-7s : %6.0f [%6.0f - %6.0f]\n", m, q[2], q[1], q[3]))
}
```

## 13.4 Null vs observed histograms

```{r perm-plot, fig.height=4, fig.width=12}
metric_labels <- c(
  n_deg  = "DEGs (FDR < 0.05, |lfc| > 0.75)",
  n_gsea = "Hallmark pathways (padj < 0.05)",
  n_tf   = "TFs (decoupleR ULM CollecTRI, p < 0.05)")

null_long <- null_df %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(n_deg, n_gsea, n_tf),
                      names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = metric_labels))

real_long <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = factor(metric_labels, levels = metric_labels),
  value  = c(real_perm$n_deg, real_perm$n_gsea, real_perm$n_tf))

p_perm <- ggplot(null_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#11335d", color = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(data = real_long, aes(xintercept = value),
             color = "#9d1939", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = real_long,
            aes(x = value, y = Inf, label = sprintf("observed = %d", value)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5, color = "#9d1939", size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = sprintf(
        "LNCaP — label-permutation null distribution (N = %d shuffles)",
        N_PERM),
       subtitle = "Treatment labels (LOY / sgCTRL) shuffled across samples; unpaired DE for both null and observed",
       x = "Count from one permutation", y = "Number of permutations") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))

print(p_perm)
save_fig(p_perm, "permutation_null_histograms", width = 12, height = 4)
```

## 13.5 Empirical p-values

```{r perm-pvalues}
emp_p <- function(real, null_vals) {
  # Right-tail empirical p (fraction of perms with null >= observed).
  # +1 in numerator and denominator is the standard small-sample correction
  # so p is never exactly 0.
  (sum(null_vals >= real, na.rm = TRUE) + 1) / (length(null_vals) + 1)
}

perm_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  metric           = unname(metric_labels),
  observed         = c(real_perm$n_deg, real_perm$n_gsea, real_perm$n_tf),
  null_median      = c(median(null_df$n_deg), median(null_df$n_gsea),
                       median(null_df$n_tf)),
  null_p10         = c(quantile(null_df$n_deg, 0.10),
                       quantile(null_df$n_gsea, 0.10),
                       quantile(null_df$n_tf,   0.10)),
  null_p90         = c(quantile(null_df$n_deg, 0.90),
                       quantile(null_df$n_gsea, 0.90),
                       quantile(null_df$n_tf,   0.90)),
  empirical_p_right = c(emp_p(real_perm$n_deg,  null_df$n_deg),
                        emp_p(real_perm$n_gsea, null_df$n_gsea),
                        emp_p(real_perm$n_tf,   null_df$n_tf)))

fwrite(perm_summary, file.path(TF_DIR, "lncap_permutation_summary.csv"))
knitr::kable(perm_summary, digits = 3,
             caption = sprintf("Permutation-null summary for LNCaP (N = %d shuffles)",
                               N_PERM))
```

**How to read this:** the null distribution shows how many DEGs / pathways /
TFs you'd typically recover from a random treatment labeling at the same
sample sizes. An empirical p-value near 0 ( = real value far above the null)
means the canonical analysis is producing signal well above what random
relabeling generates. An empirical p near 1 would mean the real result is
indistinguishable from random — i.e. the signal isn't separable from
method-level noise at this sample size.
